segments.html:
The wizard, from the goal down to the checks

Eight levels. Read top to bottom: each one zooms into the boundaries of the one above. Dashed frames are boundaries; every arrow names what crosses and the shape it has.

L0 Goal: one codebase, three ways to run it

Every way in enters through bin.ts and the cli dispatch. The cli builds the store, starts the TUI only for the interactive way, and starts one run store per agent run before calling the agent. The agent writes back only through WizardUI; the TUI renders the store; the control server serves the same store to a parent. Everything that leaves the machine is HTTPS.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
ways in → cliprocess entryargv, the API key in env, a socket pathbin.ts preflight → main.ts → dispatchProgram(config, options) picks runWizard or runWizardHeadless
cli → storesurfacethe flow to register; one run store per agent runnew FlowStore(flow); startRun(session): RunStore
cli → agentsurfacewhat to run and as whomrunAgent(runConfigFor(config), run.session, { composed })
agent → storesurfaceprogress and outcomegetUI(): WizardUI (44 methods) → StoreUI → one setter each
store → tui → storesurfacestate out, commits in ([1] only)subscribe, FlowStoreApi reads and setters
Developer → tuiprocess (TTY)keystrokes in, frames outInk stdin/stdout
Parent → store/controlprocess (unix socket, 0600)ControlState out; setters, run requests in ([3])HTTP/1.1 JSON; ControlState, RunRecord
agent → files, gatewayprocess → disk, networksource edits and env keys; model callswizard tools MCP and shell; HTTPS bearer
cli, store → PostHog APImachine → networkauth and project data; task-stream eventsHTTPS REST; no answers, no secrets

Way [2] is way [1] without the TUI: the same FlowStore, a console renderer, one run. Way [3] is way [2] plus the control server, which lets a parent set the store and start any registered program or catalog skill.

L1 Run surfaces: what each way in actually does

The TUI is unchanged. The other four surfaces are the same non-interactive pipeline or the same TUI with a control server attached. A control server never runs anything on its own: it mirrors the store and waits for a parent.

SurfaceCommand · buildWhat runsHow it ends
[1] TUInpx @posthog/wizard [command] · publishedInk render with StoreUI; OAuth in the browser; gates intro, auth; the flow's steps; one startRun + runAgent per run stepoutro, then mcp, slack-connect, keep-skills; exit 1 if the run failed
[2] headless--headless-DONOTUSE-EXPERIMENTAL --api-key --project-id --install-dir [--region] · published, hidden flagLoggingUI + HeadlessUI (console output, tasks into the store); API key → credentials, no browser; ciPreRun or the onReady walk; one runAgent; the gateway token is mintedoutro to the log; task stream pushed to PostHog unless --no-telemetry; --task-stream-log also dumps; exit 0, or 1 through wizardAbort
[2b] CI--ci --api-key --project-id --install-dir · dev builds onlythe same pipeline with build tag ci; gateway bearer from WIZARD_CI_GATEWAY_TOKEN_FILE instead of a mint; asks disabled unless --e2e-asktask stream dumped to a file (default path), never pushed; exit 0/1
[3] controlled headless--headless… --control-socket <path> · publishedStoreUI, e2eAsk on; the control server serves the store and waits; a parent detects, sets the store, and starts runs; each POST /runs is one agent on a fresh RunStore; /run and TUI actions answer 501POST /shutdown ends the process with 0; the ledger keeps every run's end state
[3b] controlled TUI--ci --control-socket <path> [--e2e-ask] · dev builds onlythe real TUI with a ci session (API key, no browser) and the control server attached; the parent commits what a keyboard would (/actions), resolves credentials (/credentials), and releases the flow's run (/run); /detect and /runs answer 501the flow ends as in [1]; the parent reads frames through a PTY
individual agentscontrolled headless, or in processPOST /runs { programId }, { skillId } (generic agent-skill), plus installDir, frameworkContext, config overlay; in process runAgent(runConfigFor(config), session)one run, one RunRecord; 409 while one is in flight

Published builds refuse --control-socket without the headless flag and never carry the control server in the TUI chunk; the smoke test audits both.

Recipes

A whole program, headless, driven over the socket. The launched program only names the flow the store registers; every run is chosen per request.

S=/tmp/w/w.sock   # a directory you own, mode 0700
POSTHOG_WIZARD_API_KEY=<personal key> node dist/bin.js --headless-DONOTUSE-EXPERIMENTAL \
  --control-socket $S --project-id 228144 --region us --install-dir /path/to/app &
curl -s --unix-socket $S http://x/health
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/detect -d '{}'                       # ciPreRun or onReady: framework, credentials
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/runs -d '{"programId":"posthog-integration"}'
curl -s --unix-socket $S 'http://x/state?wait=120000&since=17' | jq .state.session.runPhase   # long poll until it settles
curl -s --unix-socket $S http://x/runs | jq '.runs[].status'                    # wait for "done" before shutting down
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/shutdown -d '{}'                     # process exits 0, socket unlinked

Individual agents. Each POST /runs is one independent run on a fresh RunStore; a second one while the first is in flight is a 409.

curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/runs -d '{"skillId":"audit-events"}'                 # any catalog skill, on the generic agent-skill program
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/runs -d '{"programId":"metrics","installDir":"apps/web","frameworkContext":{"router":"app"}}'
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/runs -d '{"programId":"audit","config":{"allowedTools":["Read","Grep"],"requiresAi":false,"streamWorkflowId":"audit-nightly"}}'

Set the store first, then run. Setters are screen independent; GET /store lists the 25 the wire accepts.

curl -s --unix-socket $S http://x/store | jq '.setters[].name'
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/store/setFrameworkConfig  -d '{"params":{"integration":"nextjs"}}'
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/store/setFrameworkContext -d '{"params":{"key":"router","value":"app"}}'
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/store/setCredentials      -d '{"params":{"accessToken":"…","projectApiKey":"…","projectId":228144,"apiHost":"https://us.posthog.com"}}'

The real TUI under a parent (dev builds). Same store, real Ink; the parent commits what a keyboard would and reads the frame back through a PTY. This is what the snapshot route and the MCP proxy do.

POSTHOG_WIZARD_API_KEY=<key> npx tsx bin.ts --ci --control-socket $S --project-id 228144 --install-dir /path/to/app --e2e-ask
curl -s --unix-socket $S http://x/state | jq '.state.currentScreen, [.state.actions[].id]'
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/actions/confirm_setup -d '{}'
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/credentials -d '{}'    # API key → project credentials, advances auth
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/run -d '{}'            # releases the flow's own agent start
curl -s --unix-socket $S -X POST http://x/actions/answer_question -d '{"params":{"answers":{"q1":"yes"}}}'

In process. runAgent(runConfigFor(config), session, { composed }) from @agent is one run with no flow and no screens; cli/main.ts has already installed a LoggingUI.

L2 Surfaces: the import boundary

Four source roots. A surface imports another only through its public entries; instances cross the other way by injection. store imports no surface; tui and agent never meet. The compiler, an architecture suite, and a bundle audit enforce the same matrix.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
cli → storesurfacethe store class, the UI accessor, programs, the control server@store, @store/types, @store/programs; @store/control by dynamic import from two runner files
cli → agentsurfaceone agent runrunAgent(config: ProgramRunConfig, session: WizardSession, { composed? })
cli → tuisurfacethe render entry and the console renderersstartTUI → TuiHandle { store, unmount, waitForSetup }; LoggingUI, HeadlessUI
tui → storesurfacewhat screens read and commitFlowStoreApi = Pick<FlowStore, 63 names>; Flow, FlowStep; flow keys as ScreenId
agent → storesurfacehow a run reports and what it readsWizardUI (44 methods + interactive); ProgramRunConfig; ask bridge, tools
store → any surfacesurfacenothingno import; instances arrive by setUI, new FlowStore(flow), hooks

Injection closes the loop the other way: cli installs StoreUI or LoggingUI with setUI, hands FlowStore to the TUI and the control server, and hands ControlHooks to the server.

L3 Objects: what attaches to what at runtime

One FlowStore per process, one RunStore per agent run. Every writer reaches the store through one contract; every reader subscribes to one store. The agent only ever sees WizardUI and its own session copy.

L4 Data: who owns which key

A key lives in exactly one place. The flow keeps what a later run must see; a run keeps what a later run must not. The wire gets a whitelist of the merge and never a secret.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
flow → store.sessioninside storeeverything that outlives a runWizardSession map
run → store.sessioninside storethe active run's keysRUN_SESSION_KEYS (8) laid over the flow
store.session → wireprocess → socketthe reader's viewControlSession = Pick<WizardSession, 21 keys> & { hasCredentials, projectId }
never on the wireprocess → socketaccess token, API key, user record, answers, vaultcredentials reduce to a boolean; answers are recorded as ids and prompts only

The two artefact URLs (dashboard, notebook) moved to the flow after a real self-driving run showed run 2 wiping what run 1 created.

L5 Wire: the control API as the store on a socket

A route is a store question, a store setter, or one of four hooks for what the store cannot do. Screen-gated actions keep keyboard parity; named setters give a parent full store controls; a run request lays data fields over a program.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
GET /statesocketthe store, readControlState; ?wait=&since= resolves on version > since
POST /actions/:idsocketa commit legal on the current screen{ params } → one setter; same setter the key handler calls
POST /store/:settersocketa commit whatever the screen{ params } → one of 25 CONTROL_SETTERS, each a STORE_BOUNDARY_MEMBERS name
POST /runssocket → hookone independent runRunStartBody: programId or skillId, installDir?, frameworkContext?, config? (7 data fields)
GET /runssocketthe ledgerRunRecord: runId, programId, skillId, installDir, status, error, timestamps, result = ControlState at run end
POST /credentials · /detect · /shutdownsocket → hookwhat the store cannot doControlHooks; 409 while running, 501 on the other surface
errorssocketevery bad input400 param/action/setter/program, 404 route, 409 in flight, 413 > 64 KB, 415 not JSON, 500 hook, 501 surface

L6 A run: what goes in, what comes out

Independent by construction. The agent receives a run config and a session copy, speaks only through WizardUI, and its RunStore is discarded by the next run. Composition (which run after which, with what context) lives above, in the cli or the parent.

EdgeBoundary crossedCarriesShape
config → agentstore → agentwhat to runProgramRunConfig from runConfigFor(config); functions in run never cross the socket, data fields may be overlaid
session → agentstore → agentas whom and whererun.session: a copy with installDir, merged frameworkContext, skillId
agent → RunStoreagent → storeprogress and outcomeWizardUI → StoreUI → FlowStore setters → the active RunStore
gatesagent ↔ storewhen to waitwaitForAiOptIn, waitForGate(id) from postAuthGateIds; unknown ids resolve at once
outcome → parentstore → sockethow it endedRunRecord.result = ControlState at run end; runPhase settles before the record does

L7 Enforcement: what fails if a boundary moves

The same rule is checked three ways so it cannot drift in one place: the compiler, tests that scan the source, and an audit of the built chunks. Under them, one Vitest project per surface and real socket-driven runs.

Deep dive with runtime scenarios, evidence, review findings, and decisions: the canvas "Wizard surface split: architecture report" in this channel. Source PRs: PostHog/wizard #1269 to #1283.
